title: HVAC Local Services Ads: Cost, Setup and Lead Quality
html:
HVAC local services ads (LSA) are Google's pay-per-lead ads for HVAC companies: you pay when a homeowner calls or messages you, not when someone clicks. Google may also ask HVAC advertisers to accept Local Services Ads Performance Max terms during the move.

Set the weekly budget from your cost per booked job, not from the lead price alone, and finish Google's verification before you bid. HVAC owners should also set up the message button on Maps so urgent customers can text you.

When a homeowner's AC dies, the first thing on the phone screen is often a Local Services Ads block. It sits at the top of the results with a Google badge, above regular ads and map listings. That position is why HVAC owners ask what it costs and why some leads feel wasted. For organic calls alongside ads, compare HVAC SEO agencies in Houston by published price.

This guide ranks 10 tips by when you do them: setup first, then budget, then lead quality. Each tip has a cost, a step list and one mistake to avoid. Start with the first four, set your budget with tip 5, and add the rest over the first month.

HVAC LSA tips at a glance

Sorted by when you do each step, first to last. Cost shows what the step needs, not a price list.

# Tip What it costs When to do it Difficulty
1 Finish verification before you bid Staff time Week 1 Medium
2 Pick the HVAC job types you want No extra cost Week 1 Low
3 Set a service area your techs can reach No extra cost Week 1 Low
4 Build a profile that earns the call Staff time Week 1 Medium
5 Set the weekly budget from booked-job math Part of the budget Week 2 Medium
6 Raise bids ahead of heat and cold Part of the budget Seasonal Low
7 Split emergency repair and install work Part of the budget Week 2 Medium
8 Answer every call and message Staff time Ongoing Medium
9 Dispute leads that do not fit Staff time Weekly Low
10 Ask for a review after every job No extra cost Ongoing Low

HVAC LSA tips by timing, 2026. Budget amounts depend on your market.

How do you set up HVAC local services ads?

You set up HVAC local services ads by clearing Google's verification, choosing job types and a service area, and building a trusted profile. Do this before you set a budget, because ads cannot run until verification finishes.

1. Finish verification before you bid

Complete Google's screening so your ads can run. New advertisers must finish the Local Services screening and verification to earn the Google Verified badge, according to Google's Local Services Ads help page. Existing advertisers who already verified keep their badge.

  • Gather your state HVAC license, insurance certificate and business details.
  • Run the owner and tech background checks Google asks for.
  • Check each item in the LSA dashboard until none shows as pending.

Cost: staff time only. Mistake to avoid: setting a budget while verification is open, since you pay for nothing until the ads run.

2. Pick the HVAC job types you want

Turn on the job types that make you money and turn off the rest. Google lets you choose service categories, so a company that does not do duct cleaning should not pay for those leads.

  • List the jobs your techs run profitably: repair, tune-up, replacement, install.
  • Select only those categories in the dashboard.
  • Review the list each season.

Cost: no extra cost. Mistake to avoid: leaving every category on, which fills the phone with jobs you refuse.

3. Set a service area your techs can reach

Limit the service area to ZIP codes you can reach on the same day. A call from a ZIP code you cannot serve is a paid lead with no job behind it.

  • Pull a map of your tech start points.
  • Choose ZIP codes inside a drive time your dispatcher accepts.
  • Drop the fringe ZIP codes that produced no booked jobs after a month.

Cost: no extra cost. Mistake to avoid: copying your Google Ads area, which is usually wider than your real route.

4. Build a profile that earns the call

Fill every profile field so a homeowner trusts you in a few seconds. The profile shows your badge, reviews, hours and photos next to two or three competitors.

  • Add real photos of your trucks, techs and finished installs.
  • Match your hours to when a person actually answers the phone.
  • Keep the business name and phone number the same as your HVAC Google Business Profile.

Cost: staff time. Mistake to avoid: listing 24-hour service when nobody answers at night.

How much do HVAC local services ads cost?

HVAC local services ads cost a fee for each lead, which Google sets by job type and market. Hiring help adds a management fee. Check your dashboard for the real price per lead in your area instead of trusting a national average.

Cost parts for HVAC local services ads. Plan prices do not include ad spend.

5. Set the weekly budget from booked-job math

Choose a weekly budget that books jobs below your gross profit per job. The number to track is cost per booked job: total lead fees divided by the jobs you actually book.

  • Estimate gross profit per job from your last 20 invoices.
  • Track leads, booked jobs and lead fees for four weeks.
  • Raise the budget only while cost per booked job stays under gross profit.

Sample math with made-up numbers: if you pay $1,000 in lead fees and book 10 jobs, your cost per booked job is $100. If an average job leaves $600 in gross profit, that is a healthy spread.

Mistake to avoid: judging by cost per lead alone. A cheap lead that never books is expensive.

6. Raise bids ahead of heat and cold

Increase the budget one week before the first heat wave and the first cold snap. Demand jumps when a system fails, and a capped budget runs out by noon.

  • Check the 10-day forecast each Monday in peak months.
  • Lift the weekly budget before the weather turns, not after.
  • Drop it back when demand slows.

Cost: part of your budget. Mistake to avoid: leaving the same budget all year.

7. Split emergency repair and install work

Use LSA for emergency repair calls and paid search for replacement and install jobs. LSA gives you little control over keywords and landing pages, while search ads let you target a big-ticket install.

  • Keep LSA focused on repair and no-cool or no-heat calls.
  • Run Google Ads for HVAC for replacement and financing searches.
  • Compare cost per booked job for each channel monthly.

Mistake to avoid: running both channels on one shared budget with no way to see which one books the job.

Cost per lead tells you what you paid. Cost per booked job tells you if it was worth it.

How do you keep HVAC LSA lead quality high?

You keep HVAC LSA lead quality high by answering every call, disputing leads that do not fit, and collecting reviews that lift the profile. The ads send you the call, and the phone handling decides whether it becomes a job.

8. Answer every call and message

Make sure a person answers every LSA call or calls back fast. Missed calls are paid leads that go to the next company on the list.

  • Ring the LSA number to a dispatcher line with a backup number.
  • Set an after-hours route to an answering service or on-call tech.
  • Track every call with call tracking and attribution so you see which ones booked.

Cost: staff time. Mistake to avoid: sending LSA calls to a voicemail box on weekends.

9. Dispute leads that do not fit

Dispute leads that are outside your service area, job type or a wrong number.

  • Log the date, number and reason for every bad lead as soon as it comes in.
  • File the dispute in the dashboard within the window it shows.
  • Keep a monthly tally of the reasons so you can fix the cause.

Cost: staff time. Mistake to avoid: waiting until the end of the month to review leads.

10. Ask for a review after every job

Send a review request the day a job is finished. Reviews show on the LSA profile, so more recent reviews make your listing look stronger next to competitors.

Cost: no extra cost. Mistake to avoid: asking only happy customers, since a lopsided review set looks staged.

Before your LSA goes live: verified, job types set, service area set, phone answered live, review link ready, weekly budget tied to cost per booked job.

How do you turn these tips into a plan?

Turn these tips into a plan: set up in week one, set the budget in week two, and review cost per booked job every month. Do not add a second channel until LSA calls get answered.

  1. Complete tips 1 to 4 and confirm verification clears.
  2. Set the budget with tip 5, then add tips 8 to 10 for call handling and reviews.
  3. At 30, 60 and 90 days, compare cost per booked job and move budget to what books.

Broader Google Ads management can sit next to LSA once the phones are handled.

Are local services ads worth it for HVAC companies?

Local services ads are worth it when your cost per booked job stays below your gross profit per job. Calculate it by dividing lead fees by jobs booked over four weeks. Missed calls and out-of-area leads are the usual reasons the number looks bad, and both can be fixed.

How do you rank higher in HVAC local services ads?

Focus on what you control: finish verification, keep the budget high enough to run all day, answer calls live and collect new reviews every week. Google says its badge change does not alter ranking, so profile quality and responsiveness matter most.

What is the difference between LSA and Google Ads for HVAC?

Local services ads charge per lead and show a Google badge. Google Ads charges per click and lets you pick keywords, ad text and landing pages. If you also run Performance Max, note that Google may filter brand queries out of it. Many HVAC companies use LSA for emergency repair calls and Google Ads for replacement and install jobs.

Can you dispute a bad HVAC LSA lead?

Yes. You can dispute leads that fall outside your service area, job type or that are wrong numbers, using the LSA dashboard. Log each lead with the date and reason. File the dispute inside the window the dashboard shows, then review the reasons monthly.

What do you need to run HVAC local services ads?

You need a state HVAC license, insurance, business details and background checks for the owner and techs, all verified by Google. Then add a profile with photos, hours and reviews. Ads cannot run until the verification items in your dashboard are complete.

Are local services ads worth it for HVAC companies?
Local services ads are worth it when your cost per booked job stays below your gross profit per job. Calculate it by dividing lead fees by jobs booked over four weeks. Missed calls and out-of-area leads are the usual reasons the number looks bad, and both can be fixed.
###
How do you rank higher in HVAC local services ads?
Focus on what you control: finish verification, keep the budget high enough to run all day, answer calls live and collect new reviews every week. Google says its badge change does not alter ranking, so profile quality and responsiveness matter most.
###
What is the difference between LSA and Google Ads for HVAC?
Local services ads charge per lead and show a Google badge. Google Ads charges per click and lets you pick keywords, ad text and landing pages. If you also run Performance Max, note that
[Google may filter brand queries](/services/)
out of it. Many HVAC companies use LSA for emergency repair calls and Google Ads for replacement and install jobs.
###
Can you dispute a bad HVAC LSA lead?
Yes. You can dispute leads that fall outside your service area, job type or that are wrong numbers, using the LSA dashboard. Log each lead with the date and reason. File the dispute inside the window the dashboard shows, then review the reasons monthly.
###
What do you need to run HVAC local services ads?
You need a state HVAC license, insurance, business details and background checks for the owner and techs, all verified by Google. Then add a profile with photos, hours and reviews. Ads cannot run until the verification items in your dashboard are complete.
